channel.title: thenitishkr — Research, Evidence and Intelligence
channel.description: Public-interest intelligence archive: Article 12, DISHA, digital constitutional personhood, Supreme Court records, cyber evidence and accountability cases — by Nitish Kumar (thenitishkr), India.

item.title: MeitY Has 30 Days on Stolen Citizen Data — The Clock Has Run
item.dc:creator: Nitish Kumar (thenitishkr)
item.description: The Supreme Court directed MeitY on 19 May 2026 to examine the representation in W.P.(Crl.) 163/2026 concerning stolen personal data of Indian citizens held on foreign servers. Thirty days have now elapsed. This report documents what the direction required, what the record shows, and what remains publicly unresolved as of 20 June 2026.

item.title: The Real NEET Exam Leak Investigation Has Not Yet Begun
item.dc:creator: Nitish Kumar (thenitishkr)
item.description: India restricted Telegram before NEET 2026, but the harder question remains whether the State has traced the source — from devices and SDKs to stolen data pathways. The ban is a symptom. The investigation of origin has not yet begun in any documented public record.

item.title: 12 Years of NDA: Milestone Governance or Implementation Failure?
item.dc:creator: Nitish Kumar (thenitishkr)
item.description: A public-interest analysis of twelve years of NDA governance covering public finance, disaster management, digital governance, Article 12 accountability and citizen remedy in India — examined against CAG audit findings, parliamentary records and RTI disclosures.

item.title: What If the Citizen Was Never the Centre of Digital India?
item.dc:creator: Nitish Kumar (thenitishkr)
item.description: The State can locate citizens for tax, identity, data and compliance. This analysis asks why the same citizen can disappear when remedy, accountability and human review are required. Case 13 in the DISHA Intelligence Archive.

item.title: W.P.(Crl.) 163/2026 and the MeitY Digital Governance Record
item.dc:creator: Nitish Kumar (thenitishkr)
item.description: The Supreme Court routed W.P.(Crl.) 163/2026 to MeitY as a supplementary representation on 19 May 2026. This case file separates the procedural direction from the petition's broader data-sovereignty arguments and documents the adtech surveillance evidence record.

item.title: When the Certificate Outran the Ground: NITI Aayog ODF Case
item.dc:creator: Nitish Kumar (thenitishkr)
item.description: India's 2019 ODF declaration tested against NSS, NFHS-5, NARSS, CAG and public-health evidence. The case documents the gap between certification timing and ground reality, keeping NITI Aayog's amplification role distinct from the original certification chain.

item.title: Bihar SIR: When a Legitimate Objective Meets a Disputed Process
item.dc:creator: Nitish Kumar (thenitishkr)
item.description: The Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in Bihar asked existing registered voters to prove themselves again despite records already held by the State. Case 12 analyses the constitutional process question — an author conclusion, not a Supreme Court finding.

item.title: The Empty Vault: NDMA Disaster-Fund Accountability Case
item.dc:creator: Nitish Kumar (thenitishkr)
item.description: Statutory responsibility, disaster-governance documents, citizen impact and accountability questions connected to W.P.(Crl.) No. 394/2025. Case 01 in the DISHA Intelligence Archive examines utilisation certificates, CAG audit gaps and NDMA fund accountability.

item.title: The Sanitation Mirage: ODF False Justification Case
item.dc:creator: Nitish Kumar (thenitishkr)
item.description: A case record examining the gap between India's Open Defecation Free declaration and ground evidence from NSS, NFHS and CAG reports. Case 04 in the DISHA Intelligence Archive documents the evidence and separates it from political claims.

item.title: DISHA Intelligence Architecture: Evidence, Memory and Constitutional Intelligence
item.dc:creator: Nitish Kumar (thenitishkr)
item.description: DISHA (Defence Intelligence Signals Heuristic Architecture) is a six-layer evidence-first civic intelligence framework invented by Nitish Kumar on 25 April 2012. Ver 4.2.0 whitepaper documents methodology, validation limits and the claim-to-source discipline.
